# Database store: SQLite by default, Postgres optional, per-user `store.forUser(req.user)`

## What to build

graph-manager keeps all its state in one JSON file today (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`, class `DataStore`, file `<dataDir>/graph-manager.json`). Replace it with a small database layer and a per-user store, without changing any behaviour a user can see:

1. **`src/server/db/`**: a `Db` interface with two drivers. `SqliteDb` (package `better-sqlite3`, the default, file `<dataDir>/graph-manager.db`) and `PostgresDb` (package `pg`, used when `GM_DATABASE_URL=postgres://…` is set). Numbered migrations in `src/server/db/migrations/NNN-name.sql` run at startup in one transaction. This task adds `001-base.sql` (tables `instance`, `user_data`, `schema_version`).
2. **`src/server/identity.ts`** (new): `User`, `ADMIN_USER` and the Fastify request decoration `req.user`. In this task every authenticated request gets `req.user = ADMIN_USER`. Later tasks set it from accounts or a gateway header.
3. **`src/server/store.ts`**: `interface Store { instance(): InstanceData; forUser(user: User): Promise<UserStore> }`, `interface UserStore { get(): Data; update(fn): Promise<void>; reviewers(): Reviewer[] }`, `class SqlStore implements Store`. `Data` is today's `dataSchema` without `sessionSecret` and `instanceId`, which move to `InstanceData` (table `instance`).
4. **Import**: on first start with a database, an existing `<dataDir>/graph-manager.json` is imported into the user `admin` (its `sessionSecret`/`instanceId` into `instance`), then renamed `graph-manager.json.imported`.
5. **Every route** and every helper that read `ctx.store.get()` now reads `(await ctx.store.forUser(req.user))`. `AppContext.store` becomes `Store`, and `AppContext.db: Db` is added.
6. **Contract tests** run on SQLite always and on Postgres when `GM_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set. CI gets a Postgres job on ubuntu.

Do NOT change any source under `packages/graph-execution` (the engine). The only allowed change there is adding `better-sqlite3` and `pg` to `dependencies` in `packages/graph-execution/package.json`, because graph-manager ships inside that npm package (see `bundle-imports.test.ts` below). Everything else is in `apps/graph-manager` and `.github/workflows/qa.yml`.

Sibling tasks build on the names in this task, so use them exactly as written: `User`, `ADMIN_USER`, `req.user`, `Db`, `openDb`, `migrate`, `Store`, `UserStore`, `SqlStore`, `InstanceData`, `Data`, `AppContext.store`, `AppContext.db`, and migration number 001. Task "accounts" adds `002-users.sql` and task "run-archive" adds `003-runs.sql`, possibly in either order. **`migrate` must therefore apply any missing version, not only versions above the highest applied one.**

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` (lines 1–206): the whole `DataStore`. `dataSchema` (11–102), the reviewer seeding (151–156), `projects()`/`project()` (163–173), `update()` with its serial chain and rollback (179–197), and the atomic write (199–205). The new `SqlUserStore.update` must behave exactly like lines 179–197.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.test.ts` (whole file): the current behaviours (recipe migration, instance id kept, reviewer seeding, concurrent updates, rejected update keeps old data, old file without sandbox keys, invalid file errors). Port all of them.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts` (lines 39–70 `AppContext`/`BuildAppOptions`, 80–102 store open + reviewers file + `Sandboxes`, 125–137 onClose hooks): where the store is opened and passed around.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/main.ts` (lines 29–62): `startManager`. A `ConfigError` thrown here makes the process print the message and exit 1 (lines 74–77).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (lines 8–24 `Config`, 90–129 env schema and `loadConfig`): add `GM_DATABASE_URL` here. **Add to the schema; do not rewrite it**, because sibling tasks add their own variables to the same schema.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts` (lines 111–169): the auth hook (119–126) is where `req.user` gets set. `session()` (113–117) reads `sessionSecret` (now `ctx.store.instance()`) and `revokedSessions` (now the admin's `UserStore`). Login (144) signs with `sessionSecret`. Logout (156) updates `revokedSessions`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/test-helpers.ts` (lines 37–61): `appWithLogin` opens a `DataStore` and returns it as `store`. Most route tests use `store.get()`/`store.update()` from it.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/bundle-imports.test.ts` (whole file): every bare import under `src/server` must be a dependency in `packages/graph-execution/package.json`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.ts` (line 14 `MANAGER_ONLY_DEPENDENCIES`, lines 123–133 `copyEngine`): dependencies only the manager uses are not copied into sandbox containers.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (line 196 constructor, 330–333 `instanceId()`, and the `this.opts.store` uses at 385, 399, 441–442, 457, 467, 498, 507/633/656, 740–748, 778–783): `Sandboxes` reads the store synchronously.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 30–39): `resolveRunHome(workspacesDir, store: DataStore, id)` uses `store.project(pid)`.
- `apps/graph-manager/package.json` (dependencies, `build` script) and `packages/graph-execution/package.json` (dependencies, lines 58–71): `node-pty` is declared in both, and that is how a native dependency ships.
- `packages/graph-execution/scripts/bundle-manager.mjs`: copies `apps/graph-manager/dist/server` (all non-test files) into the engine's `dist/manager/server`. `.sql` files must therefore be inside `dist/server`.
- `apps/graph-manager/Dockerfile`: the build stage runs `npm ci` on `node:22-bookworm` (python3, make and g++ are present, and node-pty compiles there). better-sqlite3 installs the same way, so the Dockerfile needs no change. `GM_DATA_DIR=/data` holds `graph-manager.db`.
- `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (whole file, 18 lines): one matrix job on ubuntu, macos and windows.

Run `grep -rln "DataStore\|store\.project" apps/graph-manager/src` to find them all.

## Patterns to follow

**Serial updates with rollback (keep exactly):** `store.ts:179-197`
```ts
update(fn: (d: Data) => void): Promise<void> {
  const run = async (): Promise<void> => {
    const next = structuredClone(this.data);
    fn(next);
    const valid = dataSchema.parse(next);
    const prev = this.data;
    this.data = valid;
    try { await this.write(); } catch (err) { this.data = prev; throw err; }
  };
  const result = this.chain.then(run);
  this.chain = result.catch(() => undefined);
  return result;
}
```
`write()` becomes `UPDATE user_data SET data = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE user_id = ?` with `JSON.stringify(this.data)`.

**Config variable with a validation message:** `config.ts:90-114`. The schema uses `optional` (empty string becomes undefined), and `loadConfig` reports the first issue as `invalid <NAME>: <message>`:
```ts
GM_DATABASE_URL: optional.refine((v) => v === undefined || /^postgres(ql)?:\/\//.test(v), "must start with postgres:// or postgresql://"),
// → ConfigError "invalid GM_DATABASE_URL: must start with postgres:// or postgresql://"
...
if (e.GM_DATABASE_URL !== undefined) config.databaseUrl = e.GM_DATABASE_URL;
```
Add `databaseUrl?: string` to `Config` with a doc comment.

**Error mapping:** `ConfigError` (config.ts:29-34) stops startup with its message. A database that cannot be reached throws `new ConfigError(\`Cannot connect to the database: ${reason}\`)` from `openDb`.

**Fastify request decoration with module augmentation** (new, in `identity.ts`):
```ts
import "fastify";
export interface User { id: string; name: string; email?: string }
export const ADMIN_USER: User = { id: "admin", name: "admin" };
declare module "fastify" {
  interface FastifyRequest { user: User }
}
```
In `authRoutes` (auth.ts), call `app.decorateRequest("user", null as unknown as User)` once before adding the hook, and set `req.user = ADMIN_USER` in the `onRequest` hook right after `session(req)` succeeds (line 124). Also set `req.user = ADMIN_USER` for requests that do not need auth (line 123 returns early), so `req.user` is never null in a handler. Later tasks replace these two assignments.

**Test pattern:** temp dirs from `tempDir()` (`test-helpers.ts:10-14`), and `appWithLogin()` for route tests (`app.inject` with `headers: { cookie }`). Mirror `store.test.ts` for store tests.

## Step-by-step tasks

### ADD dependencies

- **IMPLEMENT**: `npm install better-sqlite3@^12 pg@^8 -w graph-manager`, then `npm install -D @types/better-sqlite3 @types/pg -w graph-manager`, then add the same two runtime entries (`"better-sqlite3"`, `"pg"`, same ranges, alphabetical order) to `dependencies` in `packages/graph-execution/package.json` and run `npm install` at the root so that `package-lock.json` is updated. Commit the lockfile changes with the rest.
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.ts:14` add `"better-sqlite3"` and `"pg"` to `MANAGER_ONLY_DEPENDENCIES`, so they are not copied into sandbox containers (`copyEngine`). The third test in `bundle-imports.test.ts` then requires them in the engine's dependencies, which the step above adds.
- **GOTCHA**: better-sqlite3 downloads a prebuilt binary, or compiles with node-gyp if it cannot. If the install fails, read the error; do not swap the package for something else. Node is v22 here.
- **VALIDATE**: `node -e "require('better-sqlite3')(':memory:').prepare('select 1 as x').get()"` from `apps/graph-manager`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/identity.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `User`, `ADMIN_USER`, and the `declare module "fastify"` augmentation shown above. Nothing else; task "gateway" later adds `verifyIdentity`/`signIdentity` to this file.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/db.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  ```ts
  export type Dialect = "sqlite" | "postgres";
  export interface Db {
    readonly dialect: Dialect;
    /** Rows of a SELECT (or of a statement with RETURNING). Placeholders are `?` in both dialects. */
    query<T = Record<string, unknown>>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): Promise<T[]>;
    /** A statement without rows. A string without params may hold several statements (migrations). */
    exec(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): Promise<void>;
    /** Runs `fn` in one transaction: COMMIT when it resolves, ROLLBACK when it throws. */
    transaction<T>(fn: (db: Db) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
    close(): Promise<void>;
  }
  export async function openDb(config: Pick<Config, "dataDir" | "databaseUrl">): Promise<Db>
  ```
  `openDb` returns `PostgresDb.connect(config.databaseUrl)` when it is set, otherwise `SqliteDb.open(path.join(config.dataDir, DB_FILE))`. Export `DB_FILE = "graph-manager.db"`. Both drivers wrap connection or open failures in `ConfigError("Cannot connect to the database: " + message)`.
- **GOTCHA**: values are strings and numbers only (JSON is stored as TEXT). Booleans go in as 0/1 (SQLite has no boolean; better-sqlite3 throws on `true`). Convert `true`/`false` params to 1/0 in both drivers.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/sqlite.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `class SqliteDb implements Db` over `better-sqlite3` (`import Database from "better-sqlite3"`).
  - `static open(file)` does `mkdir` of the parent dir (mode 0o700), opens the file, runs `pragma journal_mode = WAL`, `pragma busy_timeout = 5000` and `pragma foreign_keys = ON`, and chmods the file to 0o600 (skip on win32). Also accept `":memory:"` for tests (no mkdir, no chmod).
  - `query` uses `stmt.all(...params)`, or `stmt.run` when `stmt.reader` is false (then return `[]`). `exec(sql)` without params uses `db.exec(sql)` (multi-statement); with params it uses `prepare(sql).run(...params)`.
  - `transaction(fn)`: better-sqlite3 is synchronous, but `fn` is async. Serialize transactions with a promise chain (like `DataStore.update`), run `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `await fn(this)`, then `COMMIT`, or `ROLLBACK` and rethrow.
  - `close()` calls `db.close()`.
- **GOTCHA**: top-level `query`/`exec` calls made while a transaction is open on the same connection join that transaction. That is acceptable (one process), but `transaction` itself must not nest: keep a chain so a second `transaction()` waits for the first.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/postgres.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `class PostgresDb implements Db` over `pg`'s `Pool` (`import pg from "pg"; const { Pool } = pg;`).
  - `static async connect(url: string, opts: { schema?: string } = {})`: create the Pool. With `schema`, run `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "<schema>"` first and pass `options: \`-c search_path=${schema}\`` to the Pool. Tests use this so that each test gets its own schema. Then run `SELECT 1`, and turn a failure into `ConfigError("Cannot connect to the database: " + err.message)` after `pool.end()`.
  - Placeholders: convert each `?` to `$1`, `$2`, … (export `toPgParams(sql)` and unit-test it; SQL in this code base never contains a literal `?`).
  - `transaction(fn)`: `const client = await pool.connect()`, `BEGIN`, `fn(dbOverClient)`, `COMMIT`, or `ROLLBACK` and rethrow, then `client.release()` in `finally`.
  - `close()` calls `pool.end()`.
- **GOTCHA**: `pg` returns `TEXT` columns as strings. Keep every column TEXT or INTEGER so that both drivers return the same JS types. Never use `SERIAL` or `JSONB` in shared SQL.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/migrate.ts` and `db/migrations/001-base.sql`

- **IMPLEMENT** `001-base.sql` (works on both dialects):
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS instance (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_data (user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
  ```
- **IMPLEMENT** `migrate(db: Db): Promise<number[]>`: lists the files in `fileURLToPath(new URL("./migrations/", import.meta.url))`. A file name is `NNN-name.sql` (both dialects), or `NNN-name.sqlite.sql` / `NNN-name.postgres.sql` (one dialect only; pick the one for `db.dialect`). First run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)`. Then, inside one `db.transaction`, read the applied versions, apply every version that is **not applied yet** in ascending order (gaps allowed, because 002 and 003 come from parallel tasks), and insert each version into `schema_version`. Return the versions applied. Two files with the same number and dialect throw `duplicate migration NNN`.
- **IMPLEMENT** the build copy: in `apps/graph-manager/package.json` change `build` to `tsc -p tsconfig.json && node -e "require('node:fs').cpSync('src/server/db/migrations','dist/server/db/migrations',{recursive:true})" && vite build`. tsc does not copy `.sql` files, and `bundle-manager.mjs` copies `dist/server` as is.
- **GOTCHA**: Postgres allows several statements in one `query` call only without parameters. That is fine because migrations have none. For SQLite, use `db.exec(sql)`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-manager && ls apps/graph-manager/dist/server/db/migrations`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `dataSchema` = today's schema without `sessionSecret` and `instanceId`. Keep every other field and default unchanged. In particular, `revokedSessions` stays in the per-user `Data`, not in `InstanceData`; the accounts task relies on it. Keep `Data`, `Forge`, `SandboxRecord`, `SandboxLimits`.
  - `instanceSchema = z.object({ sessionSecret: z.string(), instanceId: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/) })` and `export type InstanceData = z.infer<typeof instanceSchema>`.
  - Free functions in place of the old methods: `export function projectsOf(d: Data): Project[]` (sorted by name, from lines 163–168) and `export function projectOf(d: Data, id: string): Project | undefined` (lines 170–173).
  - `export interface UserStore { readonly user: User; get(): Data; update(fn: (d: Data) => void): Promise<void>; reviewers(): Reviewer[] }`
  - `export interface Store { instance(): InstanceData; forUser(user: User): Promise<UserStore> }`
  - `export class SqlStore implements Store`:
    - `static async open(db: Db, opts: { dataDir?: string } = {}): Promise<SqlStore>`: `await migrate(db)`. Load `instance` rows (`sessionSecret`, `instanceId`). With `opts.dataDir`, run `importJsonFile(db, opts.dataDir)` first (below), so an imported secret wins. Create the missing instance keys (`randomBytes(32).toString("hex")`, `randomBytes(8).toString("hex")`) with `INSERT INTO instance (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING`, then read them back.
    - `forUser(user)`: a `Map<string, Promise<SqlUserStore>>` cache keyed by `user.id`. Load `SELECT data FROM user_data WHERE user_id = ?`. When there is no row, create one with `dataSchema.parse({})` plus `reviewers = structuredClone([...BUILTIN_REVIEWERS])` (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO NOTHING`, then select again). A stored row is parsed with `dataSchema.parse` (this migrates old sandbox recipes). When a row has no `reviewers`, seed them and write. An invalid row throws `user data of <id> is invalid: <path>: <message>; …`, in the same format as store.ts:143. On a load error, remove the cache entry so the next call retries.
    - `SqlUserStore.update` follows the serial chain with rollback shown above; `reviewers()` returns `this.data.reviewers ?? []`.
  - Remove `DataStore` from this file. Keep `DATA_FILE = "graph-manager.json"` and export it (the importer uses it).
- **IMPORTS**: `randomBytes` from `node:crypto`; `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS`, `reviewerSchema`, `type Reviewer` from `graph-execution/api`; `type Db` from `./db/db.js`; `migrate` from `./db/migrate.js`; `importJsonFile` from `./db/import-json.js`; `type User` from `./identity.js`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/import-json.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export class JsonFileStore { static async read(dataDir: string): Promise<{ instance: Partial<InstanceData>; data: Data } | undefined> }` (the old file reader, store.ts:121–149). It returns undefined when the file is missing. On bad JSON it throws `${file} is not valid JSON`, and on an invalid file `${file} is invalid: …`, both as today. It parses with `dataSchema.extend({ sessionSecret: z.string(), instanceId: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/).optional() })`, so a file without `sessionSecret` is still invalid, as today.
- **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function importJsonFile(db: Db, dataDir: string): Promise<boolean>`: when `<dataDir>/graph-manager.json` exists **and** `user_data` has no `admin` row, do the following in one `db.transaction`:
  - insert the admin row (with the data parsed by `dataSchema`, and the reviewers seeded if absent);
  - upsert `instance.sessionSecret` and, if present, `instance.instanceId`, so that existing cookies and Docker instance labels survive (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value`).
  After the commit, `rename` the file to `graph-manager.json.imported`, and return true. When `admin` already has a row, leave the file untouched and return false.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `GM_DATABASE_URL` and `Config.databaseUrl`, as in the pattern above. Add a test to `config.test.ts`: a valid URL is kept, `mysql://x` throws `invalid GM_DATABASE_URL: must start with postgres:// or postgresql://`, and an empty value means unset.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `AppContext.store: Store` and a new `AppContext.db: Db`, always set in `buildApp` (later tasks, such as accounts and run archive, use `ctx.db`). `BuildAppOptions.store?: Store` and `db?: Db` (tests pass an in-memory SQLite from `memoryDb()`; see test-helpers below).
  - In `buildApp`: `const db = opts.db ?? (await openDb(config))`. Set `ctx.db = db`. Then `const store = opts.store ?? (await SqlStore.open(db, { dataDir: config.dataDir }))`, and `app.addHook("onClose", () => db.close())` only when buildApp opened the db itself.
  - `const admin = await store.forUser(ADMIN_USER)`, then `writeReviewersFile(config.dataDir, admin.reviewers())`. The reviewers file is still one per instance, written from admin's list. Leave a `// TODO(hosted-sessions): per-user reviewers file` comment.
  - `new Sandboxes({ config, store: admin, instanceId: store.instance().instanceId })`.
- **GOTCHA**: `buildApp` is also called by many tests through `appWithLogin`. Each gets its own temp data dir, and therefore its own SQLite file.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: change the constructor opts to `{ config: Config; store: UserStore; instanceId: string; docker?; platform? }`. `instanceId()` returns `this.opts.instanceId`. Every other `this.opts.store.get()/update()` stays as is (the `UserStore` has the same `get`/`update`). Line 783: `resolveRunHome(…, this.opts.store, …)`. Sandboxes stay instance-wide and use the admin's settings for now; add `// TODO(hosted-sessions): per-user sandbox settings` at the constructor.

### UPDATE helpers: `runhome.ts`, `liverun.ts`, `forges.ts`, `pr.ts`, `project-pr.ts`, `proxy.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: give every helper the caller's `UserStore` instead of reading `ctx.store`:
  - `resolveRunHome(workspacesDir, us: UserStore, id)` uses `projectOf(us.get(), pid)`.
  - `liveRunIn(ctx, us, home)`, `connFor(ctx, us, kind)`, `clientFor(ctx, us, kind)`.
  - `prStatus(ctx, us, ws, runId)`, `preparePr(ctx, us, …)`, `runPrJob(job, ctx, us, …)`, `startPr(ctx, us, …)`, and the private `suggest`.
  - `projectPrStatus(ctx, us, home, runId)`, `startProjectPr(ctx, us, home, runId)`, and the private `gather`, `repoRows`, `othersOf`, `runProjectPrJob`.
  - `proxy.ts:84`: `resolveRunHome(ctx.config.workspacesDir, await ctx.store.forUser(req.user), wsId)`.
- **GOTCHA**: PR jobs run after the response is sent (`runPrJob`), so pass the `UserStore` object, not `req`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `session()` reads `ctx.store.instance().sessionSecret` and `(await ctx.store.forUser(ADMIN_USER)).get().revokedSessions`, so it becomes async.
  - Login signs with `ctx.store.instance().sessionSecret`.
  - Logout updates the admin's `revokedSessions`.
  - Add the `decorateRequest` call and the `req.user = ADMIN_USER` assignments described above.

### UPDATE every route module in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/`

- **IMPLEMENT**: for each line in the list above, at the top of the handler: `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(req.user);`, then `us.get()`, `us.update(…)`, `us.reviewers()`, `projectsOf(us.get())`, `projectOf(us.get(), id)`. Pass `us` to the helpers. Handlers written as `async () =>` need `async (req) =>`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no database settings, graph-manager creates `<dataDir>/graph-manager.db` (mode 600 on Linux and macOS), runs migration 001 and works as before: login, Settings, Reviewers, Runs, forges, sandbox settings and projects all read and write the database.
- [ ] An existing `<dataDir>/graph-manager.json` is imported into user `admin` on first start and renamed `graph-manager.json.imported`. Every setting, PR record, reviewer and project survives. Old session cookies stay valid (same `sessionSecret`), and `instanceId` is unchanged.
- [ ] `GM_DATABASE_URL=postgres://…` uses Postgres. `GM_DATABASE_URL=mysql://x` fails at startup with `invalid GM_DATABASE_URL: must start with postgres:// or postgresql://`. An unreachable database fails with `Cannot connect to the database: <reason>` (exit 1).
- [ ] Migrations run twice without error, and `migrate` applies a missing lower version even when a higher one is applied.
- [ ] `Store`/`UserStore`/`SqlStore`, `Db`/`openDb`/`SqliteDb`/`PostgresDb`, `User`/`ADMIN_USER`, `req.user`, `AppContext.store: Store` and `AppContext.db: Db` (set in `buildApp`), `BuildAppOptions.db?: Db`, and the test helpers `memoryDb()`, `testStore()` and `openTestStore(dataDir)` exist with exactly these names.
- [ ] Every route reads state only through `await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)` (or `ADMIN_USER` in `/api/internal/*`). `store-usage.test.ts` enforces it.
- [ ] Two users never see each other's data through `forUser`.
- [ ] The contract suite passes on SQLite locally, and on Postgres in the new `postgres` CI job.
- [ ] No file under `packages/graph-execution` changes except the two added `dependencies` entries in its `package.json`.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-manager`
